page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv5 server family. It is configured with 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The server features 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. It includes 154 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1890.49 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1630.0. However, due to the physical limitation of a single core supporting two threads, multi-core performance is poor, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1878.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 1933.27. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, registering poor results for both small-block cached reads at 104.76 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 14.31 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high density of memory relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for workloads that require a large memory workspace without demanding heavy parallel processing. The inclusion of 154 GB of local storage adds value for temporary data caching. It is best suited for memory-intensive, low-compute workloads such as small database instances, caching layers like Redis, and lightweight web serving.
